'''''Silaum silaus''''', commonly known as '''pepper-saxifrage''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a [[perennial]] plant in the family [[Apiaceae|Apiaceae (Umbelliferae)]] (the carrot family) found across south-eastern, central, and western Europe, including the British Isles. It grows in damp grasslands on neutral soils.

== Description ==
''Silaum silaus'' is an erect, [[Glabrousness#In botany|glabrous]] [[umbellifer]]<ref name="wildlifetrust">{{cite web | url=http://www.wildlifetrusts.org/species/pepper-saxifrage | title=Pepper Saxifrage | publisher=[[The Wildlife Trusts]] | accessdate=28 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029235114/http://www.wildlifetrusts.org/species/pepper-saxifrage | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref> with woody, stout and cylindrical [[tap roots]], which are hot and [[aromatic]].<ref name="spook" /> ''S. silaus'' has dark grey or black [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] at the top; petiole remains are found at the bottom of the stem, which is solid<ref name="spot">{{cite web | url=http://www.naturespot.org.uk/species/pepper-saxifrage | title=Pepper-saxifrage - ''Silaum silaus'' | publisher=NatureSpot | accessdate=28 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202420/http://www.naturespot.org.uk/species/pepper-saxifrage | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref> and [[:wikt:striate|striate]].<ref name="spook" /> Its [[umbels]] are 2–6 cm in diameter, are [[:wikt:Terminal#Adjective|terminal]] or axillary, and compound, with 4 to 15 angled rays of 1–3 cm; the [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] is larger than the rays, and both are [[:wikt:papillose|papillose]]. The flowers are mostly [[hermaphroditic]].<ref name="spook" />

''Silaum silaus'' has 2–4-[[pinnate]] leaves, which have a triangular<ref name="spot" /> and [[lanceolate]] outline, a long petiole and the primary divisions are long-stalked.<ref name="spook" /> [[Segmentation (biology)|Segments]] are 10–15 mm long, shaped from lanceolate to linear, the ends are [[acuminate]] or obtuse and [[:wikt:mucronate|mucronate]], the leaves are finely [[:wikt:serrulate|serrulate]], with a prominent [[Leaf#Divisions of the blade|midrib]]; the apex is often reddish in colour.<ref name="spook" /><ref name="spot" /> There are 1-[[pinnate]] upper [[:wikt:cauline|cauline]] leaves present, which are either simple or reduced to a sheath; there is no petiole and the [[cotyledons]] are tapered at the base.<ref name="spook" /> There are 0–3 [[bracts]] and 5–11 [[:wikt:bracteole|bracteoles]]; the [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]] are linear-lanceolate with [[:wikt:scarious|scarious]] margins.<ref name="spook" />

The flowers are yellowish and 1.5 mm across,<ref name="spot" /> with absent [[sepals]], and the styles form a [[:wikt:stylopodium|stylopodium]].<ref name="spook" /> The fruits are 4–5 mm in size, oblong-ovoid, and are rarely compressed.<ref name="spook" /> The [[commissure]] is broad, the [[:wikt:mericarps|mericarps]] are prominent with slender ridges and lateral forming narrow wings; a [[:wikt:carpophore|carpophore]] is present.<ref name="spook" /> There are numerous [[:wikt:vitta#English|vittae]], with stout [[:wikt:pedicel|pedicels]] of 2–3 mm in size, and the stigmas are [[:wikt:capitate#Adjective|capitate]].<ref name="spook" />

==Taxonomy==
''Silaum silaus'' was one of the many species described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in volume 1 of the 1753 edition of his ''{{lang|la|[[Species Plantarum]]}}'' as ''Peucedanum silaus''.<ref>{{cite book | chapter=Tomus I | chapter-url=http://botanicus.org/page/358265 | title=[[Species Plantarum]] | publisher=Laurentius Salvius | author=Linnaeus, Carl | authorlink=Carl Linnaeus | year=1753 | location=Stockholm | page=246 | archiveurl=https://archive.today/20240526221302/https://www.webcitation.org/6LTPvRTxU?url=http://botanicus.org/page/358265 | archivedate=26 May 2024}}</ref> It was given its current binomial name in 1915 by Swiss botanists [[Hans Schinz]] and [[Albert Thellung]].

The [[etymology]] of the genus name ''Silaum ''is uncertain, although it may refer to the mountainous plateau [[La Sila]] in southern [[Italy]].<ref name="Gledhill2008">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NJ6PyhVuecwC&pg=PA353 | title=The Names of Plants | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | accessdate=29 October 2013 | last=Gledhill | first=D. | year=2008 | edition=4 | pages=353– | isbn=9780521866453}}</ref>  Another possible explanation is that ''Silaum'' may be derived from the yellow [[ochre]], related to the colour of the plant's flowers.<ref name="spook" /> ''Silaus'' is an old generic name<ref name="Gledhill2008" /> used by [[Pliny the Elder|Pliny]].<ref name="spook" />

''Silaum silaus'' bears the common name pepper-saxifrage (with or without hyphenation) despite being neither a [[saxifrage]] nor peppery in taste.<ref name="emorsgate">{{cite web | url=http://wildseed.co.uk/species/view/126 | title=''Silaum silaus'' – Pepper Saxifrage | publisher=Emorsgate Seeds | accessdate=29 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131101003106/http://wildseed.co.uk/species/view/126 | url-status=dead | archivedate=1 November 2013}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Silaum silaus'' is found in western, central and south-eastern [[Europe]]<ref name="nordica">{{cite web | url=http://www.floranordica.org/Review/-Review_public/accounts/Silaum.html | archive-url=https://archive.today/20131030100657/http://www.floranordica.org/Review/-Review_public/accounts/Silaum.html | url-status=usurped | archive-date=October 30, 2013 | title=''Silaum'' | publisher=Flora Nordica | date=7 August 2008 | accessdate=28 October 2013 | last=Fröberg | first=Lars }}</ref> (including [[Great Britain]]),<ref name="spook" /> north to the [[Netherlands]] and [[Sweden]] but is absent from [[Portugal]].<ref name="spook" /> In Great Britain, it is found mainly south of the far south of [[Scotland]].<ref name="bsbi">{{cite web | url=http://www.bsbimaps.org.uk/atlas/map_page.php?spid=1916.0 | title=Hectad map of ''Silaum silaus'' (Pepper-saxifrage) in GB and Ireland | publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] | accessdate=28 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195254/http://www.bsbimaps.org.uk/atlas/map_page.php?spid=1916.0 | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref> The species is listed as an [[invasive species]] in [[Denmark]].<ref name="isc">{{cite web | url=http://www.cabi.org/isc/?compid=5&dsid=117125&loadmodule=datasheet&page=481&site=144 | title=''Silaum silaus'' | work=[[Invasive Species Compendium]] | date=26 May 2011 | accessdate=28 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029200540/http://www.cabi.org/isc/?compid=5&dsid=117125&loadmodule=datasheet&page=481&site=144 | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref>

''Silaum silaus'' grows in a wide variety of habitats, generally preferring those with damper soils.<ref name="wildlifetrust" /> Specifically, ''S. silaus'' can be found in [[Grassland#Biodiversity|unimproved neutral grassland]], railway and [[road verges]]<ref name="spot" /> and [[meadows]] (hay,<ref name="wildlifetrust" /> water<ref name="atlas">{{cite web | url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=node/408 | title=''Silaum silaus'' (Pepper-saxifrage) | work=Online Atlas of the British & Irish Flora | accessdate=28 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029202841/http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=node/408 | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref> and lowland meadows<ref name="bap">{{cite web | url=http://jncc.defra.gov.uk/Docs/UKBAP_BAPHabitats-29-Lowland%20Meadows.doc | title=Lowland Meadows | publisher=[[UK BAP]] | work=UK Biodiversity Action Plan Priority Habitat Descriptions | accessdate=28 October 2013 | author=BRIG (ed. Ant Maddock) | year=2008 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195940/http://jncc.defra.gov.uk/Docs/UKBAP_BAPHabitats-29-Lowland%20Meadows.doc | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref>); it is also occasionally found on [[Downland|chalk downs]] and vegetated [[Shingle beach|shingle]].<ref name="atlas" />

== Ecology ==
[[File:Papilio machaon egg (3695270849).jpg|thumb|Egg of the butterfly ''[[Papilio machaon]]'' on a ''Silaum silaus'' host plant]]
''Silaum silaus'' is an indicator of agriculturally unimproved meadows,<ref name="wildlifetrust" /> and is part of a group (in the [[United Kingdom]]) of flowering plants specially associated with neutral grassland associated with low-nutrient regimes.<ref name="bap" /> This group is declining in the UK due to agricultural improvement, diffuse pollution and [[habitat fragmentation]]<ref name="wildlifetrust" /> and hence ''S. silaus'' is on the [[United Kingdom Biodiversity Action Plan]].<ref name="bap" /> At least three species of [[moth]] [[larvae]] in the UK use the plant as a food source – ''[[Sitochroa palealis]]'', ''[[Agonopterix ciliella]]'' and ''[[Agonopterix yeatiana]]''.<ref name="moths">{{cite web | url=http://www.northumberlandmoths.org.uk/foodplants.php?foodplant=Silaum%20silaus | title=Moths larvae that feed on Pepper-saxifrage ''Silaum silaus'' | work=[[Northumberland]] Moths | accessdate=28 October 2013 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029211338/http://www.northumberlandmoths.org.uk/foodplants.php?foodplant=Silaum%20silaus | url-status=live | archivedate=29 October 2013}}</ref>

''Silaum silaus'' fruit has been identified from substage III of the [[Hoxnian interglacial]] period (a stage in the middle [[Pleistocene]]) in the British Isles.<ref name="Godwin1956">{{cite book | url=https://archive.org/details/historyofbritish0000godw | url-access=registration | title=The History of the British Flora: A Factual Basis for Phytogeography | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press|CUP]] Archive | accessdate=29 October 2013 | last=Godwin | first=Sir Harry | authorlink = Harry Godwin | year=1956 | pages=[https://archive.org/details/historyofbritish0000godw/page/227 227]– | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103142658/http://books.google.com/books?id=n205AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA227 | url-status=live | archivedate=3 January 2014}}</ref>

== Uses ==
''Silaum silaus'' is listed in [[John Parkinson (botanist)|John Parkinson]]'s 1640 work ''Theatrum Botanicum'' as being able to soothe "frets" in infants.<ref name="Hatfield2004">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2GGz6708nqgC&pg=PA81 | title=Encyclopedia of Folk Medicine: Old World and New World Traditions | publisher=[[ABC-CLIO]] | accessdate=29 October 2013 | last=Hatfield | first=Gabrielle | year=2004 | pages=81– | isbn=9781576078747 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140103144617/http://books.google.com/books?id=2GGz6708nqgC&pg=PA81 | url-status=live | archivedate=3 January 2014}}</ref>
